verdict.root_cause: productcatalogservice's GetProduct path fails on a feature-flag condition: every ERROR-status GetProduct span has exactly one child call to hipstershop.FeatureFlagService/GetFlag, the flag child itself is not in error, and the ERROR is first set on the productcatalogservice handler wrapping that lookup — the handler is reading a flag value and turning it into a returned gRPC error. Sibling GetProduct calls in the same traces that skip the flag lookup succeed at ~0ms, and ListProducts is unaffected, so this is a selective flag-conditioned error injection, not a service-wide fault [tr_00905b37520e]. No deploy, image, or env change is recorded for productcatalogservice in 24h [tr_a8da2f7fa5b8], consistent with a flag value held outside the seed service's change scope. The wrong flag value is itself what breaks the request, so the remedy is reverting that flag state.
verdict.reasoning: Traces are the only dispatch producing causal structure rather than an absence: error status originates on the productcatalogservice handler, exclusively on spans containing a GetFlag child, under both frontend and checkoutservice parents, while flag-free siblings succeed [tr_00905b37520e]. That is a conditional error branch keyed on a configured value — the value's wrongness is the mechanism. Latency excludes the waiting story (root spans ~1.4-11.9ms, flag child sub-2ms), and bad_deploy has nothing to roll back since no change is recorded for the service [tr_a8da2f7fa5b8]. The cartservice apply/revert chaos loop was all reverted before onset and its cart/Redis spans carry no error, so it explains nothing here [tr_5ee8a8764cab]. The metric dispatches claim no sustained error elevation, but both baselines overlap the same ~8-10% error floor, so a flat comparison cannot rebut a per-request error branch seen directly in traces; frontend and loadgenerator alerts follow as caller-ward propagation.
open_questions: No trace covers the 19:01:45 onset — all returned traces fall 19:03:26-19:03:37, so the mechanism is confirmed only for the late window [tr_00905b37520e].
The feature-flag service was never queried: who set the flag, when, and its current value are unknown (the unmeasured edge).
Logs returned nothing due to a label mismatch, and latency/CPU/memory/restart series were never returned, so resource exhaustion is unexamined rather than excluded [tr_204783be290e, tr_1ced1f16f25d].

alternatives.root_cause: The feature-flag service itself is serving a wrong flag value and productcatalogservice is faithfully obeying it.
alternatives.why_not: Same flag state and same fix, but the flag child spans carry no error and the failure is materialized by productcatalogservice's own handler branch; the flag service was never queried, so blaming it is unevidenced.

alternatives.root_cause: productcatalogservice is intermittently saturated (CPU, memory, or connections) and errors coincide with flag-lookup spans by chance.
alternatives.why_not: Saturation would not sort errors perfectly by presence of a flag child while sub-millisecond siblings succeed; no saturation series was returned either way.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so nothing should change: productcatalogservice GetProduct spans that carry a hipstershop.FeatureFlagService/GetFlag child will keep being marked ERROR at the handler, sibling GetProduct calls without the flag child will keep succeeding at ~0ms, and ListProducts will stay clean. The next investigative step is a change_history and current-value query against the feature-flag service, which this proposal does not perform.
proposal.if_wrong: Abstention is wrong if a change-history query against the feature-flag store returns a recorded prior flag value with a change timestamp inside the incident window — that would satisfy revert_config's two preconditions and make a targeted flag revert the correct action. It is also wrong if the flag value is proven to be held in productcatalogservice's own environment rather than in an external flag service, since that would make productcatalogservice a legal revert_config target. Neither is shown today: the change log for productcatalogservice is empty across ~24h and explicitly rules out both a config edit and a flag flip on this service [tr_a8da2f7fa5b8], so there is no recorded prior configuration to restore. The entity that actually holds the wrong value — the feature-flag service — is not in this incident's blast radius and therefore is not a legal target for any action here.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that the flag-conditioned errors continue to reach frontend and checkoutservice for as long as it takes a human to query and revert the flag; the mechanism is confirmed only for the 19:03:26–19:03:37 window and the 19:01:45 onset is unverified by traces, so the true duration and rate are unknown. The risk of NOT abstaining is worse and concrete: revert_config on productcatalogservice would recreate the container with the same configuration (there is no prior config recorded), producing an unnecessary outage that changes nothing; restart_service would discard cache and also leave the external flag value untouched, and the evidence points at a value read at request time rather than at process state; rollback_image has no prior image tag and no deploy in the window to roll back to.
proposal.blast_radius: Unchanged by this proposal. The failing path continues to be seen by frontend and checkoutservice, which are the observed gRPC parents of the ERROR-status GetProduct spans, and by the root HTTP spans above them; recommendationservice's ListProducts path and adservice/cartservice are unaffected. Had an action been taken on productcatalogservice, those same two callers plus loadgenerator-driven root requests would have seen connection resets during the container recreate.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical severity with simultaneous productcatalogservice and frontend alerts plus loadgenerator impact indicates a real user-facing failure, not a quiet world. Productcatalogservice is the likely origin but the alerts alone do not distinguish a bad deploy from resource exhaustion.
